consolidate:
What in stored memory is duplicated, disagrees with itself, or has gone out of date — answered in one call, with the full text of every claim involved. It decides nothing and changes nothing.

Reach for it whenever the question is about the store itself rather than about a subject: what is redundant in here, is anything contradicting itself, what is worth cleaning up before handing a project over, has memory got noisy. `recall` cannot answer those. It ranks claims by how well each one matches a query, so three phrasings of a single claim come back as three separate hits with nothing saying they are the same claim — the comparison is the part `recall` leaves to you, and it is what this does.

There is no subject filter, and that is the point: every live claim in the space is compared against every other one, which is the only way a duplicate is found at all. Asked about one subject, call it anyway and read the lists for that subject — each candidate carries its entities, tags and full text, so you can judge it here instead of looking it up.

Three lists come back:

- `near_duplicates` — groups of live claims saying the same thing. Merge a group by calling `remember` with the one wording worth keeping and `supersedes` set to the id it replaces. Read `min_similarity` before you do: it is the weakest pair anywhere in the group, not the weakest link, so a low number means the group chained together through a middle claim and may not be one claim at all.
- `contradictions` — pairs about the same subject that are close without being the same. Nothing here has judged that they disagree; read both and decide. When one of them is wrong, send the right one with `supersedes` set to the wrong one's id.
- `stale_contexts` — claims filed as short-lived that recall has kept alive far past the point their class would have expired them. If one turned out to be durable, store it again with a slower `decay_class`; if it was only scaffolding for one session, `forget` it.

Every list can be empty, and usually some are — an empty answer means there is nothing worth your attention, not that the call failed. `scanned` says what was actually compared.

This looks in the current space only, unlike every other read here: a tidy-up should not reach the shared user space unless you name it with `space`.
